author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: These parsers read Keeper Security ARAM events, one event per line in Keeper's Syslog file format. Keeper's external logging writes them to an Amazon S3 bucket, which a Sophos NG-SIEM S3 Ingest integration reads. Logins, Admin Console logins and failed logins go to Auth, and every other event goes to CloudAudit with the event code.
notes:
Setup:
- Needs the Advanced Reporting and Alerts Module (ARAM).
- In the Keeper Admin Console, set up external logging to an Amazon S3 bucket with file format Syslog and read the bucket with a Sophos NG-SIEM S3 Ingest (customer-managed) integration: each line is one event.
- Keeper's TCP syslog push uses the same line format, but it only connects to ports 514 or 6514 (TLS, with a valid CA-signed certificate), which the data collector's documented ports (UDP 514, TCP 601) don't match, so it needs a relay.
- Keeper already ships Sentinel, Splunk and CrowdStrike integrations; this covers Sophos NG-SIEM.

Field mapping:
- Logins, Admin Console logins and failed logins go to Auth; every other event (record use, sharing, roles, policies, BreachWatch, MSP and managed company changes) goes to CloudAudit with the event code.

Made up in the samples:
- Samples follow the syslog examples on Keeper's S3 and syslog pages, with event codes from its event descriptions page; the header host is changed to an example domain (Keeper sends its own) and all values are made up.

Testing:
- Each child, combined with the parent into one parser, passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-13 (65 of 65 fields matched the emulator), and the parent's confirm string picked the same lines there.
- On 2026-10-14 each child also passed Run Test in a lab tenant as a separate parser under its parent.
- No built-in parser claimed these lines in 5 Run Tests.
